chapter: Return to New York and the Embers
title: Sammy Burke proposes a small group and Ben Bart turns him down
summary: Recording around Broadway for small labels, he met agent Sammy Burke, who advised forming a quartet; Universal's Ben Bart refused him as too experienced, so Burke quit his job to manage him personally.

bands.name: Ina Ray Hutton and Her Orchestra

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: So in the meantime, I had this paper and looking at it, and so, fooling around down Broadway, you know, as usual, walking around seeing the different guys, you know, making a little record here and there. I forget the guy we made the records with. We were making a lot of stuff with Coleman Hawkins and Foots Thomas, who used to be with Cab, and Barefield, and all those. Joe something was his name. Put out a whole series of eight tracks there for awhile. I mean 78s. And I'm looking for something, looking around, and I recorded for Him sometimes on Keynote, and Commodore. And I happened to run into Sammy one day, Sammy Burke. He's the guy that was Irving Mills, who was I think the biggest agent around here at one time, you know. Sammy told me they had about 100 bands, Ina Ray Hutton, Larry Clinton, Duke and Cab and a whole host of bands. Clyde McCoy, and he was booking everything in there. So I run into him, and he says, 'Hey, how you doing,' you know. I knew him from Cab and I had seen him every now and then, when I was back in the '30s with --

Stuff, yeah. So now we get to talking on the street, and he like loves to walk up Broadway, at that time, anyhow. I walk with him, and he says, 'Look, you know what I'd like for you to do? I'd like for you to -- I was thinking you could get you a group together, I think about three pieces. Get

about four altogether. You and bass, piano and drums." He said, "Now, forget about the big bands. It's all over. Let me see what I can do for you." He said, "You've been a nice guy. I've been watching you for years. You always carried yourself nice and never got mixed up in the dope angle and you always tried to support your family. Let me see what I can do." At this time he's with Universal, with Ben Bart. So now he said, "Let me talk to Ben. Let me talk to Ben." So he called me and said, "Ben wants you to come down and talk to him." So I come down and Ben was asking me, "What are you doing?" And I named all the bands, like I told you, out west, and different stuff, and with Cab and Lunceford and Stuff and different groups, Benny Carter, and so he says, "Well, okay. Maybe you'll hear from me. I'll see what we can do here." So I says, "All right, I'd appreciate it." So I left, and then Sammy called me and said, "Oh, nothing happened." I said, "What happened?" He said, "He come in and said, 'That guy's been around too long. He'll be asking too many questions. That guy's been around. He should be working up here. He'll ask too many questions.'" So Sammy says, "I'm going to quit, and just handle you myself." And I thought this was real great, you know, right off, starting off.
Right off, you know, he says, "I'm going to quit up there and just handle you myself, nobody but you."
And I said, "Well, I appreciate anything that you can come up with, you know."
